question: What claim about the range of languages is at stake in distinguishing heard and unheard forms of varied speech?
premises: Languages of varied form are present in this context.
Some of those forms are heard and others are unheard.
The distinction between heard and unheard is asserted as a real difference.
inference: The field of speech includes both heard and unheard languages of varied form.
uncertainties: It is unclear whether the distinction is perceptual or ontological.
plain_english: Languages of varied form indeed arise, both heard and unheard.
